title: Runtime Sentinels: Tunable SLO Cutovers for Canary & Shadow Deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a flexible, tunable runtime 'Sentinel' that monitors composite SLO signals during canary, A/B and shadow experiments and triggers automated cutovers (rollback/freeze/evacuate) based on configurable, model- and route-scoped policies. The goal is to provide operators with fine-grained control over sensitivity (false positive/negative trade-offs), apply blended signals (latency, p50/p95, error-rate, per-token cost, throughput) and provide an offline tuner to suggest thresholds from historical traffic replays.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime Sentinels can be attached to any rollout and evaluate a weighted composite score from at least latency, error_rate, token_cost, and throughput.
Operators can author cutover policies: immediate rollback, staged evacuation, traffic freezing, or alert-only. Policies support per-route overrides.
Automatic action executed within configured SLO windows and documented in rollout audit logs; actions include traffic reversion and model pinning to previous stable version.
An offline tuner produces recommended thresholds for a given route/model using historical traffic replay; recommendations surface as suggested policy presets in the Console.
End-to-end integration tests exist that simulate regressions (latency spike, token-cost jump, error burst) and verify the Sentinel triggers correct policy within expected time bounds.
Dashboard panels show composite score, contributing signals and recent Sentinel actions.
design_notes: Introduce a lightweight 'Sentinel Engine' sidecar in the control plane that ingests per-route metric streams (aggregates from metrics pipeline) rather than raw traces to keep runtime overhead low.
Composite score is computed as weighted z-scores to normalize heterogeneous signals. We expose both absolute and relative modes (relative uses baseline performance for the pinned model).
Threshold tuner uses a Bayesian optimization loop over historical replays; output is a small set of candidate presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive).
Actions are expressed as immutable 'policy-blobs' associated with rollout objects. Execution path is idempotent and records decision rationale into audit log for compliance.
Safety: every automated cutover must be reversible, provide operator notification, and have a short 'grace window' where rollback is marked as tentative until confirmation or time expiry.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement Sentinel Engine + policy API; exercise on internal staging routes using synthetic traffic (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (canary): deploy to canary traffic for a small set of low-risk public routes; use alert-only and dry-run modes for 1 week while collecting telemetry.
Phase 3 (limited-auto): enable rollback actions behind feature flag for non-critical customers; monitor for 2 weeks and tune thresholds.
Phase 4 (GA): expose presets in Console, enable by default for new rollouts with conservative preset and operator override.
test_plan: Unit tests for composite score math (z-score normalization, weight configs, relative/absolute modes).
Integration tests: end-to-end canary flow with synthetic regression scenarios (latency spike, token-cost increase, error bursts).
Chaos test: simulate delayed metrics and missing signals to validate fail-open behavior and operator alerts.
Replay tests: use past 30 days of anonymized traffic for tuner to generate thresholds and validate on holdout slices.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana panels: Sentinel composite score time-series, per-signal contribution breakdown, recent policy actions (with links to audit logs).
Pager rule for repeated Sentinel-triggered rollbacks within an hour (indicates tuning required).
Console banner when a Sentinel action is in tentative state with link to operator actions (confirm/revert).
migration_notes: Existing rollouts continue using current rollback mechanism until opt-in. Add migration job to convert simple threshold rules to policy-blobs when project enables Sentinels.
Metrics pipeline must guarantee 10s-30s latency for aggregated signal delivery to maintain responsiveness; coordinate with observability infra (dependency ENG-41234).
